mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 30 days, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.25% and remains above this level for two consecutive months, it signals a shift from emergency monetary policy to a more neutral stance, which typically precedes a slowdown in equity market gains and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has been above 0.25% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the consumer price index (CPI) and decline in the federal funds rate indicates a policy response to inflationary pressures, which typically leads to increased market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors reassess growth and inflation risks.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS declines simultaneously, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 7.5%), a sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs per month signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 7.5%, SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS rises above 100,000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening demand for residential construction, which typically leads to increased economic activity and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST rises, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0 and remains below this level for three consecutive months, it signals a contraction in manufacturing output that typically precedes a slowdown in economic growth and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO has been below 95.0 for three consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand and housing market strength, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate sustained economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where RSAFS and HOUST both rise, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.5 percentage points in one month signals the onset of a labor market slowdown that typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5pp in a month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
